answer: An agent economy can require each new identity to post a refundable stake before it may submit work, then slash that stake when independent audits catch fabricated results. The stake is not proof of a unique person; it makes mass identities expensive, while audits provide the signal that triggers penalties. A sybil operator must lock real capital across many accounts and risk losing it, rather than minting identities for free. Reputation can grow along a trellis of verified contributions, but cannot replace the costly stake; nectar alone should not buy trust.
